name: Gibbs Hall
use: Small traditional residence hall, 111 students; Lower Quad; 'The Clubhouse' sports and active-living theme

facts.text: Dedicated June 14, 1947 and named for William D. Gibbs, New Hampshire College president 1903-1912, who broadened the college's role for the whole state.
Built 1946; one of the three Lower Quad halls with Engelhardt, Gibbs and Hunter.
Hall of 111 students at 4 Quad Way; 'The Clubhouse' sports and active-living theme.
Amenities listed are a kitchen, laundry, indoor bike storage and WiFi; no air conditioning or elevator is listed. Accessibility: none listed.

verdict: Twin of Engelhardt: a tidy 1946 Lower Quad hall with a dormered top floor, friendly but without A/C.
notes: No renovation history found for the Lower Quad halls. Old row credited Eric T. Huddleston as architect; no source I opened confirms it, so architect is left null. Licensed photo (2013) shows a long two-storey brick block with a white-clad dormered third storey and hipped roof, plain but tidy, behind the sand volleyball court mentioned by Housing. No interior photos.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a long, neat brick block behind a volleyball court.
